sections.eyebrow: Stripe reports, one for each reader
sections.title: Stop building the Monday report.
sections.lead: Monday, 9am. The board wants one page. Support wants the failed payments. Your CFO wants retention. Today someone builds all three by hand. SaasReport builds each one from your Stripe data, in the order that reader cares about, and sends it on a schedule.
sections.note: Pre-launch. Be one of the first companies we build this for.

head.title: The same month. Ten different questions.

items.title: Monday, 9am
items.text: The board wants one page. Support wants the failed payments. The CFO wants retention. Someone opens Stripe and starts three exports.

items.title: The sheet nobody trusts
items.text: Numbers get pasted, filtered and renamed on the way. Two people pull the same month and get two answers.

items.title: One view for everyone
items.text: The Stripe Dashboard is built for the person who runs Stripe. Everyone else asks that person for a screenshot.

head.title: One set of numbers. One report per reader.

steps.title: Install the app in Stripe.
steps.text: SaasReport asks for read access only. It never moves money and never changes your account.
steps.example: It reads subscriptions, charges, refunds, disputes and application fees.

steps.title: Pick who gets what.
steps.text: Choose a reader, a report and a schedule. Each report says which schedules it supports.
steps.example: CEO / Founder: Recurring revenue health, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual. CFO / Finance lead: Recurring revenue health, weekly, monthly, quarterly, annual

steps.title: Code computes every number.
steps.text: Each figure follows a published definition. Rules turn the figures into findings, with the evidence beside them. AI words the summary and never writes a figure.
steps.example: Net revenue retention was 81.08%: existing customers brought in less revenue than they did at the start of the period.

steps.title: Each reader gets a link.
steps.text: The email names the report and carries no figures. The link is signed, it expires, and you can revoke it.
steps.example: The report is a PDF stored under your own tenant.

sections.title: Seen the number? Let us build the reports instead.

head.title: If you take payments through Stripe, one of these is you.

items.title: Subscription businesses
items.text: Recurring revenue, retention and churn for the CEO, CFO, board and investors, plus new customers for sales and marketing. Reports: Recurring revenue health, Retention and churn, Sales performance, New customers, Board pack and Investor quarterly. Needs Stripe Billing subscriptions.

items.title: Merchants without subscriptions
items.text: Payments, refunds and disputes for finance and support. Reports: Refunds and returns and Payment health. They read charges, refunds and disputes only, so no subscriptions are needed.

items.title: Marketplaces and platforms
items.text: What the platform earns, and how its refunds and disputes behave. Report: Marketplace health. Stripe lets an app on a platform read only the platform's own data. Your merchants install SaasReport on their own accounts, and you can recommend it. That is a referral, not a data feed.

head.eyebrow: How a report reaches a person
head.title: A signed link, not an attachment.
What we promise, and where each promise stands.

items.title: Planned
items.text: The Stripe App requests only read permissions and never creates, changes or deletes anything in the customer's Stripe account, and never moves money.

items.title: Planned
items.text: SaasReport does not receive, store or process card numbers or bank account numbers.

items.title: Planned
items.text: Each customer's data is stored and read only under that customer's own tenant identifier; one customer cannot read another's data.

items.title: Planned
items.text: Every figure in a report is computed by deterministic code from Stripe data under published definitions; AI-written text is checked so that it contains no figure the code did not compute.

items.title: Planned
items.text: The AI provider receives only computed aggregates and never customer names, email addresses or other personal data from the customer's Stripe account.

items.title: Planned
items.text: After the customer uninstalls the app, the data derived from their Stripe account is deleted within the period stated in the privacy policy.

items.title: Planned
items.text: Report emails are sent only through SaasReport's own mail service on Cloudflare, and each carries the legal footer.

items.title: Planned
items.text: The website sets no cookies other than those strictly necessary, and runs no third-party advertising or tracking scripts.

items.title: Planned
items.text: SaasReport does not sell personal data, and does not use a customer's Stripe data to train AI models or to build benchmarks for other customers.

items.title: Planned
items.text: All traffic between Stripe, SaasReport's services, and report recipients' links uses encryption in transit.

items.title: Planned
items.text: Findings and recommendations in a report come from published rules applied to computed figures, not from AI judgement; each cites the figures that triggered it, and the thresholds are not benchmarks against other companies.

items.title: Planned
items.text: Reports are delivered as signed, expiring links to files stored under the customer's own tenant, and a link can be revoked.

items.a: Not yet. The engine that computes the numbers is built and tested. The Stripe app, the report pages and the email delivery are not. Ask for early access and we will tell you when we start building for you.

Nothing is stored yet, because nothing is built. The design is: read-only access, data kept under your own tenant identifier, encryption in transit, and no use of your data to train AI. Each promise is a commitment in the register above with its status.
A person sees a report only if their Stripe role already lets them see the data behind it. A role we do not know sees nothing. Try it in the Trust section.

It cannot. Code computes every figure. The AI is meant to write only the sentences around them, and a guard rejects any sentence that holds a number the engine did not compute. The guard exists in code. Try it in the Trust section.
Only what the reports need: subscriptions, charges, refunds, disputes and application fees. It reads nothing today.
We have not set prices. Early-access companies help us decide what is fair.
There is no date. We will not invent one. Early access is how we choose what to build first.

items.q: What can it not tell me?
items.a: Anything Stripe does not hold. Across the readers above that includes profit, cash in the bank, burn and runway, costs and expenses, profit and loss, cash balance outside Stripe, headcount and pipeline. SaasReport will not pretend to know them.

items.q: I run a marketplace. Can I see my merchants' numbers?
items.a: Not through SaasReport. Stripe lets an app installed by a platform read only the platform's own data. Merchants can install SaasReport on their own accounts, and you can recommend it.

items.q: Is it in the Stripe App Marketplace?
items.a: No. It is not listed there.
